subject: Server kills NIMBLE processes right befor producing results. Any help?

messages.author: 8a8be4e743854ad4
messages.subject: Server kills NIMBLE processes right befor producing results. Any help?
parts:
Dear all, 
I'm new to this community and a brand-new NIMBLE user (still struggling along the way)!
Please, forgive me in advance if this is off-topic or if some important information is missing in the text. I'll be happy to provide them!
Basically, I'm seeking your help to understand and hopefully fix, what is killing my  NIMBLE processes on the server I'm using.
I'm using a Ubuntu 20.04.2 LTS (version Focal Fossa) of 64 GB of RAM, 20 CPU, and 10 core. This should be a nice and relatively powerful machine, but every time I run my model the process starts, and then it gets killed when the calculation is done, right before producing the results (please see attached). I have run demanding analyses before with jags and I have never had this problem.
Looking on the internet, I have found that the Kernel of my machine may activate an OOM_Killer (Out-of-Memory Killer) which terminates the processes that are too computational demanding.
I can get some results limiting the number of iterations and number of chains, but I would need to make my analyses sounder (at least 600.000 iterations, 3 chains, and 50.000 burn-in). The funny thing is that I can run a longer model on my laptop (200.000 iterations, 1 chain) which is way less powerful than the server (RAM is 16 GB).
Generally, I think that the problem is limited to the use of NIMBLE.
Has this ever happened to any of you? Do you have any suggestions to solve this limitation? 
Thank you very much in advance!
Cheers,
Ilaria

messages.author: b252c8306d50e349
messages.subject: Re: Server kills NIMBLE processes right befor producing results. Any help?
parts:
Hi Ilaria,

I would like to check on a couple of things:

1. In the screenshot I saw an error and the "In system(cmd) : 'make' not found"; however it looks to me that that is  only commented text in the R script, and the model is compiling correctly right?

2. Have you checked in with server admin? Rather than NIMBLE per se, it could be that the server operating system is imposing a process limit or some kind of quotas. 

Hope this helps at least to exclude some possibilities!

Best, 

Sally

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Server kills NIMBLE processes right befor producing results. Any help?
parts:
Hi Ilaria,

It looks like you're running out of memory. I see you are saving 150,000 samplers for one chain. How many individual parameters are you saving for each iteration? The amount of memory used just for saving the samples will be 8 bytes per number multiplied by 150,000 and then by the number of parameters. However, if you ran the same MCMC on your laptop and didn't run out of memory, that would be strange, unless as Sally says there is some memory limit imposed on processes on the server.

-chris
